NoteTexAccessor::macro_subs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::macro_subs(std::int64_t max_passes = 1) const

Substitute Local Zero-Argument Macros¶

macro_subs() collects simple zero-argument macro declarations from each cell, removes those declarations, and substitutes matching control-word uses in the remaining source. It supports the local \newcommand, \renewcommand, and \def forms represented by the TeX cleanup kernel. Each cell owns its own macro map; a declaration in one lane never changes another lane.

One pass performs one substitution level. If \A expands to \B and \B expands to done, the default result still contains \B; passing 2 reaches done. This round-based rule is deterministic and independent of declaration or hash-table iteration order. Substitution stops early when a round makes no change, so a generous bound does not force needless scans after convergence.

The scanner respects control-word boundaries. Declaring \A does not rewrite the prefix of \Alpha, and a doubled backslash is retained as a linebreak rather than treated as a macro use. Parameterized macros, conditionals, TeX category-code changes, and file-level scope are outside this focused operation; use it for explicit local textual substitutions rather than as a TeX engine.

max_passes must be positive. The bound also prevents an endlessly recursive definition from running forever: self- or mutually recursive macros stop after the requested number of rounds. The operation returns a new shape-preserving Text Note, leaves the receiver unchanged, preserves undefined input, and rejects non-text dtypes. Each round is a single lexical pass over each cell.

Example 1: Default One-Level Substitution¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\newcommand{\A}{\B}\newcommand{\B}{done}Value: \A; prefix: \Alpha.)");
std::cout << source.tex().macro_subs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Value: \\B; prefix: \\Alpha."

Declarations are removed, \A advances one level, and the longer \Alpha control word remains intact.

Example 2: Bound Recursive Expansion Explicitly¶

std::cout << source.tex().macro_subs(2) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"Value: done; prefix: \\Alpha."

Example 3: Macro Maps Are Cell-Local¶

const auto lanes = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\newcommand{\unit}{kg}mass: \unit)",
    R"(\newcommand{\unit}{m}length: \unit)"});
std::cout << lanes.tex().macro_subs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["mass: kg", "length: m"]

Example 4: Reject A Meaningless Pass Bound¶

try {
  (void)source.tex().macro_subs(0);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "macro_subs(0): rejected\n";
}

Output¶

macro_subs(0): rejected

Negative values are rejected by the same rule.

Example 5: Undefined And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().macro_subs().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().macro_subs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "macro substitutions Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
macro substitutions Int64: rejected
